newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES STABLE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted little changed from Tuesday's levels in fairly active trade on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said the maturity of grain bills on Tuesday had lent liquidity to the system and most players were looking to re-invest their money in treasury bills, which were selling on the open market at 22.8 percent.

Dealers said the market had so far paid scant attention to the on-going strike action by the majority of Zimbabwe's civil servant over pay hikes, but did not rule out long-term negative repercussions if the issue was not resolved soon.

Meanwhile, 30-, 60- and 90-day NDCs were on Wednesday being bought at a stable 24 percent and sold at 23.5 percent from 23 percent, while bankers acceptance bills were buying and selling unchanged at 23.5 and 23 percent respectively.
Call money rates were also quoted steady at around 22.5 percent, with the central Reserve Bank indicating a start-off market surplus of Z$254 million compared to Tuesday's Z$360 million.
